Compact card lookup

35,892 Oracle IDs from the 2026-11-21 snapshot. Plain JSON, with at most 8 card records per data response.

  1. Take the full card name. Apply Unicode NFKD, lowercase, and keep only a–z and 0–9. Lightning Bolt becomes lightningbolt. If nothing remains, use other as the full key.
  2. Fetch its first four characters, or the entire key if shorter, followed by .json. For Lightning Bolt, open ligh.json.
  3. If the response contains routes, use the full key to find the file. For Lightning Bolt, open ligh-3.json. If the first file contains cards, use it directly.
  4. In every cards response, compare the full card name and keep only exact name matches. Normalization selects a file, and several different names can share that file or key. Check ambiguousNames. When several Oracle IDs match, return them all or ask for the Oracle ID.
  • No exact match: A successfully retrieved JSON file has no matching route key or no matching full card name. If the first JSON file could not be retrieved, check the linked file index. If the index loads and omits that prefix or file, the snapshot has no match.
  • Unverified: A listed file, a routed file, or the index page needed to check a missing prefix could not be read. A failed request or a 404 alone does not establish absence.
  • Tokens and emblems: Search for these in the Card Explorer or use the compressed token catalog. They are outside the scope of this compact lookup. For example, the exact name Treasure can match a non-token record here.

Each face includes the source Oracle text. A format missing from the status lists is unreported. Snapshot statuses do not capture all printing-level or commander-specific restrictions. catalogManaValue describes the card in the source. catalogFaceManaValue describes the face in the source. Game rules determine the value in a particular zone or state.
